rows.grounds: compound epithet naming a perpetually moist divine form; nitya = constant, klinnā = wet or moistened

items.question: What enduring state of moistness characterizes this named aspect of the goddess?
premises: The epithet combines constancy with wetness.
The form is designated as perpetually moist.
This moistness is presented as an abiding quality.
items.inference: The goddess is identified by an unceasing state of wetness as her defining characteristic.
uncertainties: Whether the moistness is meant ritually, cosmologically, or as a specific deity-name emphasis is not explicit in this token alone.
items.plain_english: She is Nityaklinnā, the ever-wet one.
